```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Overview

We explore demographic (age, marital, job, education) and financial health
(default, balance, housing, loan) variables against term deposit subscription,
using the training split only.

```{r}
#### Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
#### Load data
bank_df <- read_csv('../data/processed/bank_train.csv')

head(bank_df)
```

## Target variable

```{r}
#### TARGET: term deposit subscription
bank_df |>
  rename(is_deposit = y) |>
  count(is_deposit) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

The target is imbalanced: only about 12% of clients subscribed.

# Part 1: Demographic variables

```{r}
#### Filter the columns age, marital, job, education and the target column y
bank_demo_df <- bank_df |> select(age, marital, job, education, y) |>
  rename(is_deposit = y)

head(bank_demo_df)
```

## Age

```{r}
#### AGE
bank_demo_df |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(age, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(age, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(age, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_demo_df, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = 'lightgrey') +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Number of clients",
    title = "Distribution of client age"
  )
```

Age is right-skewed, ranging from 18 to 95 with a median of 39.

```{r}
bank_demo_df |>
  group_by(is_deposit) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(age, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(age, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(age, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_demo_df, aes(x = age, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Age by term deposit subscription"
  )
```

```{r}
#### AGE GROUPS
bank_demo_df |>
  mutate(age_group = cut(
    age,
    breaks = c(17, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, Inf),
    labels = c("18-25", "26-35", "36-45", "46-55", "56-65", "66+")
  )) |>
  count(age_group, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(age_group) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
bank_demo_df |>
  mutate(age_group = cut(
    age,
    breaks = c(17, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, Inf),
    labels = c("18-25", "26-35", "36-45", "46-55", "56-65", "66+")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Age group (years)",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Term deposit subscription by age group"
  )
```

Subscription is U-shaped by age: about 25% for ages 25 or younger, 9% for ages 36-55,
and 43% for ages over 65.

## Marital status

```{r}
#### MARITAL
bank_demo_df |>
  count(marital) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
bank_demo_df |>
  count(marital, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(marital) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_demo_df, aes(x = marital, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Marital status",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Term deposit subscription by marital status"
  )
```

Most clients are married (60%). Single clients subscribed most (15%) and married least (10%).

## Job

```{r}
#### JOB
bank_demo_df |>
  count(job) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

```{r}
bank_demo_df |>
  count(job, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(job) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
#### Order jobs by subscription rate so the plot is easier to read
job_order <- bank_demo_df |>
  group_by(job) |>
  summarise(rate = mean(is_deposit == "yes")) |>
  arrange(rate) |>
  pull(job)

ggplot(bank_demo_df, aes(y = factor(job, levels = job_order), fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Proportion",
    y = "Job type",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Term deposit subscription by job type"
  )
```

Students (29%) and retirees (23%) subscribed most; blue-collar workers (7%) least.

## Education

```{r}
#### EDUCATION
bank_demo_df |>
  count(education) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
bank_demo_df |>
  count(education, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(education) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_demo_df,
       aes(x = factor(education, levels = c("primary", "secondary", "tertiary", "unknown")),
           fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Education level",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Term deposit subscription by education level"
  )
```

Subscription rises with education: 9% (primary), 11% (secondary), 15% (tertiary).

# Part 2: Financial health variables

```{r}
#### Filter the columns default, balance, housing, loan and the target columns of y
bank_fin_df <- bank_df |> select(default, balance, housing, loan, y) |>
  rename(is_deposit = y)

head(bank_fin_df)
```

## Credit default

```{r}
#### DEFAULT
bank_fin_df |>
  count(default) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
bank_fin_df |>
  count(default, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(default) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_fin_df, aes(x = default, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Credit default",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Term deposit subscription by credit default status"
  )
```

Under 2% of clients are in default; they subscribed at 6% vs 12% for others.

## Housing loan

```{r}
#### HOUSING LOAN
bank_fin_df |>
  count(housing) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
bank_fin_df |>
  count(housing, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(housing) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_fin_df, aes(x = housing, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Housing loan",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Term deposit subscription by housing loan status"
  )
```

Clients without a housing loan subscribed at 17%, over twice the rate of those with one (8%).

## Personal loan

```{r}
#### PERSONAL LOAN
bank_fin_df |>
  count(loan) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
bank_fin_df |>
  count(loan, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(loan) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_fin_df, aes(x = loan, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Personal loan",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Term deposit subscription by personal loan status"
  )
```

Clients with a personal loan subscribed at 7% vs 13% for those without.

## Combined loan burden

```{r}
#### ANY LOAN (housing or personal)
bank_fin_df |>
  mutate(any_loan = if_else(housing == "yes" | loan == "yes", "yes", "no")) |>
  count(any_loan, is_deposit) |>
  group_by(any_loan) |>
  mutate(perc = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
```

```{r}
bank_fin_df |>
  mutate(loan_status = case_when(
    housing == "yes" & loan == "yes" ~ "Both loans",
    housing == "yes" ~ "Housing loan only",
    loan == "yes" ~ "Personal loan only",
    TRUE ~ "No loans"
  )) |>
  group_by(loan_status) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    subscription_rate = round(mean(is_deposit == "yes") * 100, 2)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(subscription_rate))
```

Clients with no loans subscribed at 18% vs 8% for those with at least one.

## Account balance

```{r}
#### BALANCE
bank_fin_df |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(balance, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(balance, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    perc_negative = round(mean(balance < 0) * 100, 2)
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_fin_df, aes(x = balance)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = 'lightgrey') +
  labs(
    x = "Average yearly account balance (euros)",
    y = "Number of clients",
    title = "Distribution of account balance (zoomed in)"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2000, 15000))
```

Balance is strongly right-skewed (median 450, mean 1,370 euros), and 8% of clients are negative.

```{r}
bank_fin_df |>
  group_by(is_deposit) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(balance, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(balance, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    perc_negative = round(mean(balance < 0) * 100, 2)
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_fin_df, aes(x = balance, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Average yearly account balance (euros)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Account balance by term deposit subscription"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1000, 10000))
```

```{r}
ggplot(bank_fin_df, aes(x = is_deposit, y = balance, fill = is_deposit)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(
    x = "Term deposit subscription",
    y = "Average yearly account balance (euros)",
    fill = "Term deposit subscription",
    title = "Account balance by term deposit subscription (zoomed in)"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1000, 5000))
```

Subscribers have a higher median balance (710 vs 420 euros), but the distributions overlap heavily.

```{r}
#### BALANCE vs DEFAULT
bank_fin_df |>
  group_by(default) |>
  summarise(
    median_balance = median(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_balance = mean(balance, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

Clients in default have a median balance of -5 euros, so credit default and account balance overlap.

# Summary of findings

- **Demographics:** age (U-shaped) and job show the biggest differences; education and marital status matter less.
- **Financial health:** having any loan or a default is associated with lower subscription; higher balance is associated with slightly higher subscription.
